bib.title: Defending Against Neural Fake News
bib.venue: 33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019)

question: How realistic can controllable neural fake news be, and how can it be detected, given an adversary and a verifier with few examples of that adversary's output?
hypothesis: The best generators of neural disinformation are also the best discriminators of it, because a left-to-right discriminator shares the generator's inductive bias and can find sampling artifacts.
contributions: Grover, a controllable multi-field news generator (domain, date, authors, headline, body)
RealNews, a 120GB news corpus from Common Crawl
Human study showing Grover-rewritten propaganda is rated more trustworthy than human-written propaganda
Discriminator study in a semi-supervised setting: Grover is the best detector of Grover text
Analysis of exposure bias and nucleus-sampling artifacts, with a release strategy

method.summary: Grover is a GPT2-architecture LM trained on RealNews with randomly partitioned metadata fields so any field can be generated from the others. Generations from Grover-Mega at several nucleus p values are used to train discriminators (Grover, GPT2, BERT, FastText) to separate human from machine news, in paired and unpaired settings. Humans rate Grover output on MTurk.
method.task: controllable news article generation and machine-text detection

datasets.name: RealNews
datasets.size: 120 gigabytes without compression after deduplication; 5000 news domains
datasets.split: Common Crawl Dec 2016 to Mar 2019 for training; April 2019 articles for evaluation
datasets.source: Common Crawl dumps, limited to the 5000 news domains indexed by Google News
datasets.preprocessing: Newspaper Python library extracts body and metadata; deduplicated

datasets.name: Discrimination set (April 2019)
datasets.split: 10k train (5k per label), 2k validation, 8k test; generations and human articles cut to 1024 BPE tokens
datasets.preprocessing: machine articles generated from the metadata of 10k April 2019 articles

other.discriminator_init: iteration 700k checkpoint, [CLS] token at end of article, linear layer for Human/Machine

models.name: GPT2 (124M, 355M)
models.architecture: pretrained transformer LM, newly added [CLS] token

other.used_as: discriminator and as LM baseline in Fig 3

models.name: BERT-Base / BERT-Large (cased)
models.context: 512 extended to 1024 by new position embeddings 513-1024

training.objective: cross-entropy of predicting tokens of field set F1 then F2 (random disjoint partition of fields); each field dropped with prob 10%, all but body dropped with prob 35%. Discriminators: cross-entropy on Human/Machine label
training.optimizer: Adafactor (generator); beta1 = 0.999, update clipping to RMS at most 1. Discriminators: Adam for BERT, Adafactor for GPT2 and Grover
training.lr_schedule: linear warm-up then decay over remaining iterations (generator)
training.epochs: roughly 20 epochs through the news dataset (generator); 5 (BERT discriminator); 10 (GPT2 and Grover discriminators)
training.regularisation: auxiliary language modelling loss with coefficient 0.5 for GPT2 and Grover discriminators
training.compute: about $25k for Grover-Mega at $0.30 per TPU v3 core-hour and two weeks; data collection $10k in AWS credits

other.grid_search: discriminator hyperparameters chosen after an initial grid search (grid not given)

inference.decoding: Nucleus (top-p) sampling; sample until the field-specific end token
inference.top_p: 0.96 for human study; search over {0.9, 0.92, 0.94, 0.96, 0.98, 1.0} for discriminator pairs; 0.95 for appendix examples; uniform in [0.9, 1.0] per article for weak-supervision generations
inference.samples: one generation per metadata item; 10k generated for discrimination; 100 articles per category in the human study
inference.prompting: context fields in the order domain, date, authors, headline, body, then the start token of the target field

parameters.top_p_selection: the pair's reported test accuracy uses the p with the lowest validation accuracy

other.top_k: stated in a footnote that nucleus sampling produced better and less-detectable generations than top-k in early experiments; k not given

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: over the article body only, unconditional or conditioned on all metadata, on April 2019 articles

metrics.name: Unpaired accuracy
metrics.definition: classify single articles independently as Human or Machine

metrics.name: Paired accuracy
metrics.definition: given a real and a machine article with the same metadata, the machine one must get the higher Machine probability

metrics.name: Human rating
metrics.definition: style, content and overall trustworthiness on a 1-3 Likert scale by three annotators per article

eval.protocol: single run per cell; no seeds or confidence intervals reported for accuracy; human-rating difference tested (p = 0.01); human raters are qualified Amazon Mechanical Turk workers

prompts.text: Is the style of this article consistent? 3. Yes, this sounds like an article I would find at an online news source. 2. Sort of, but there are certain sentences that are awkward or strange. 1. No, it reads like it's written by a madman.

Does the content of this article make sense? 3. Yes, this article reads coherently. 2. Sort of, but I don't understand what the author means in certain places. 1. No, I have no (or almost no) idea what the author is trying to say.

Does the article read like it comes from a trustworthy source? 3. Yes, I feel that this article could come from a news source I would trust. 2. Sort of, but something seems a bit fishy. 1. No, this seems like it comes from an unreliable source.

evidence.quote: we search over p P t.9, .92, .94, .96, .98, 1.0u.

results.claim: Grover used as a discriminator detects Grover-Mega text with about 92% accuracy with 5000 machine examples, versus 73% for the best other pretrained discriminators as stated in the text.
results.setup: Grover-Mega generator at its most adversarial top-p; April 2019 articles; discriminator trained on 5k generations plus unlimited real news
results.quote: Grover, when used in a discriminative setting, performs even better at 92% accuracy
results.note: Table 1 gives 91.6 for Grover-Mega vs Grover-Mega unpaired; the 73% does not appear as an unpaired cell for Grover-Mega generations (best other unpaired cell is GPT2 355M at 70.1, BERT-Large 68.0), so it may be the paired or another setting; the text does not say.

results.claim: Grover-Mega discriminating Grover-Mega generations reaches 91.6% unpaired accuracy.
results.setup: Table 1, discriminator Grover-Mega 1.5B, generator 1.5B, most adversarial p by validation
results.table: Table 1, row Grover-Mega, column Unpaired generator 1.5B

results.claim: Rewritten by Grover-Mega, propaganda's overall trustworthiness rises from 2.19 to 2.42 out of 3.
results.quote: The overall trustworthiness score of propaganda increases from 2.19 to 2.42 (out of 3) when rewritten by Grover.
results.note: Statistically significant at p = 0.01 per footnote 9. Machine-written propaganda is consistent with the headline at 2.64 of 3 vs 2.85 for human.

results.claim: Discrimination is hardest for nucleus p roughly between 0.94 and 0.98, depending on the discriminator.
results.setup: Grover-Mega generations; discriminators Grover-Mega, Grover-Large, BERT-Large; Fig 7
results.quote: The results indeed show a sweet spot, roughly between p“0.94 and p“0.98 depending on the discriminator, wherein discrimination is hardest.

results.claim: Grover-Mega's conditional perplexity on April 2019 article bodies is 8.7, and conditioning on metadata lowers perplexity by 0.6 to 0.9 points.
results.setup: April 2019 RealNews body field, conditional setting (all metadata)
results.quote: with Grover-Mega obtaining 8.7 perplexity in the conditional setting
results.note: GPT2 models of the same size are over 5 perplexity points worse than Grover-Base and Grover-Large.

results.claim: A larger generator drops Grover discriminator accuracy below 81%; a larger discriminator exceeds 98%.
results.setup: Table 1, Grover discriminators vs Grover generators of three sizes
results.quote: If a larger generator is used, accuracy slips below 81%; conversely, if the discriminator is larger, accuracy is above 98%.

results.claim: With weak supervision from Grover-Large, 16 to 256 Grover-Mega examples give about 78% accuracy versus about 50% without it; accuracy converges to about 92% with more Grover-Mega examples.
results.n: 5000 total training generations, x from Grover-Mega
results.setup: Grover-Mega discriminator; missing 5000-x generations from a weaker Grover with p uniform in [0.9, 1.0]
results.quote: weak supervision with between 16 and 256 examples from Grover-Large yields around 78% accuracy, while accuracy remains around 50% without weak supervision

results.setup: $0.30 per TPU v3 core-hour, 256 cores, two weeks
results.quote: at a cost of $0.30 per TPU v3 core-hour and two weeks of training, the total cost is $25k

limits: Only the threat model of a whole article generated from minimal context is studied; comments, edits to real articles, images and video are not.
Discriminators use distributional features, not evidence; no fact checking.
The result that Grover detects Grover depends on the verifier seeing generations from the same generator family; a model trained on its own predictions or generating in any order may evade it.
Adversarial Filtering did not work well for 1024-token sequences.
Discrimination was limited to 1024 BPE tokens; longer length made discrimination easier.
Single runs; no seeds or intervals for accuracy.
Human raters judge style and plausibility, not truth; false positives on real news and social biases mean humans must stay in the loop.

terms.definition: targeted propaganda that closely mimics the style of real news, generated by a neural language model
models maximizing Equation 1 are trained only conditioned on human-written text, never on their own generations
unpaired classifies single articles; paired gives a real and a machine article with the same metadata and requires a higher Machine probability for the machine one

code.snippet: The probability of observing a human-written article where all tokens are drawn from the top-p% of the distribution is p^n, where n is the document's length.
